description:
Parnell's GAA Club runs a GAA nursery, known as Nippers, for children aged 4 to 7 at their clubhouse on Main Street in Coolock, Dublin 5.

Sessions take place on Saturday mornings and introduce young children to Gaelic football and hurling fundamentals through fun, age-appropriate games in a friendly club environment.

As a community GAA club, Parnell's nursery is a good starting point for local children to build coordination, teamwork and confidence before progressing to underage teams.

Coolock Kenpo Karate Club teaches Kenpo karate to children aged 5 to 15 at the Scout Hall in Coolock Village, Dublin 5.

The club is part of the same Kenpo Karate network as Ballinteer Kenpo Karate Club, following a consistent curriculum that builds discipline, self-defence skills and fitness through structured belt progression.

Classes suit a wide age range, from young beginners through teenagers, in a supportive local setting.

Bohemian FC Academy runs a small-sided games football programme for children from U8 to U12 at the Oscar Traynor Centre in Coolock, Dublin 17.

Small-sided formats give young players more touches of the ball and more involvement in play than traditional 11-a-side games, helping develop technical skills, decision-making and match confidence.

Run under the Bohemian FC academy banner, the programme offers local children a pathway into football coaching at a well-known Dublin club's training base.

Astropark Coolock offers multi-activity summer camps for children aged 5 to 12 at its facility on Oscar Traynor Road / Coolock Lane, Dublin 17.

Camps combine a range of sports and activities across the day, giving children a varied, active way to spend school holidays while meeting new friends in a supervised group setting.

Located in the Coolock area of Dublin 17, Astropark provides a convenient camp option for families in the surrounding neighbourhoods.

Olympus Dance & Music School offers a broad mix of classes for young children at Unit 10C, Ringuard House in the Malahide Industrial Estate, Dublin 17, including preschool dance, Fitnastix gymnastics, and music and art sessions.

Having several disciplines under one roof means families can introduce children to movement, rhythm and creative activities without committing to a single specialism early on.

The preschool dance and gymnastics classes are geared toward building coordination and confidence, while the music and art sessions add a creative outlet alongside the more physical classes.

Larkhill Karate Club teaches karate to children from age 4 through to 15 and up, based at Unit 4, Santry Hall Industrial Estate in Santry, Dublin 9.

Students are grouped by age and ability into Lions, Dragons and Panthers classes, allowing younger beginners and older, more experienced students to train at a level suited to them.

The club's structure supports steady progression over several years, building discipline, focus and self-defence skills as children move up through the age groups.

Grange Gymnastics Club is a Gymnastics Ireland member club based at Unit 10D, Airways Industrial Estate on Boeing Road in Santry, Dublin 9.

Classes cater for a wide span of ages, from toddlers right through to adults, giving families a long-term gymnastics option as children grow rather than having to switch clubs.

Membership with Gymnastics Ireland means the club follows recognised gymnastics pathways and standards for participants at every level.

Thunderstruck Stage School's Santry branch offers stage school classes covering both dance and drama for children and young people aged 2.5 to 19, at Unit 5, Santry Hall Industrial Estate, Dublin 9.

The wide age range, from toddlers to young adults, allows children to stay with the school long-term, moving through different class levels as their skills and confidence develop.

Combining dance and drama training gives students a rounded grounding in performance, useful whether they're pursuing stage school for fun, confidence-building, or a future in performing arts.

Starlights GFC runs a GAA nursery called Little Stars for children aged 3 to 7 at St Pappan's Parochial Hall in Santry village, Dublin 9.

Sessions take place on Saturday mornings from 10am to 11am, giving young children an early, low-pressure introduction to Gaelic games through play-based activities.

As the club's nursery programme, Little Stars is designed as a first step for the youngest members before they progress into Starlights' underage teams.

Sportslink's Aqua Tots programme offers parent and baby swim classes for children from around 3 to 36 months at Furry Park on Swords Road in Santry, Dublin 9.

Parent-and-baby swimming at this age focuses on water confidence and gentle bonding time in the pool, with a parent or guardian in the water throughout each session.

The Aqua Tots classes give very young children an early, supported introduction to the water before they move on to more independent swimming lessons.

Finglas Celtic FC runs a football academy for children aged 4 to 7 at their grounds on Kilshane Road in Finglas West, Dublin 11.

Sessions are held on Friday evenings and Saturday mornings, giving families a choice of times to fit young children's introduction to football around the rest of the week.

As an academy aimed at the youngest age group, the programme focuses on basic ball skills, movement and enjoyment of the game rather than competitive play.

Kobukan Kobudo Renmei's Finglas branch teaches Kobudo, the traditional Okinawan martial art of weapons training, to children aged 5 to 12 at Meakstown Community Centre on Lanesborough Park, Dublin 11.

Kobudo classes typically build coordination, focus and discipline through structured weapons forms and drills, offering a martial arts option distinct from more common striking-based styles.

The Finglas classes give local children access to this less widely available discipline within the Kobukan Kobudo Renmei network.

House of Swag's Finglas branch, at 2D Century Business Park, Dublin 11, offers dance, drama and gymnastics classes for children aged 4 and up, running on Mondays.

As a newer branch of the same company behind House of Swag Swords, it follows the same combined approach of movement, performance and gymnastics skills in one class rather than splitting them across separate schools.

The Monday sessions suit children looking for a single after-school class that covers dance, acting and gymnastics basics together.

FKFT Dance School's Finglas branch offers dance classes for children and young people aged 3 to 18, held on Mondays at the W.F.T.R.A Hall in Finglas, Dublin 11.

The broad 3 to 18 age range means dancers can stay with the school from their first pre-school steps through to their teenage years, progressing through classes as they grow.

With sessions concentrated on Mondays, it offers a straightforward weekly dance class for families in the Finglas area.

Axis Ballymun, on Main Street in Ballymun, Dublin 9, hosts drama classes for children aged 7 to 16 on Tuesdays and Fridays.

The same venue is also home to Beldance Irish Dancing and En Pointe Ballet, so families visiting Axis can choose between drama, Irish dancing and ballet as separate classes running at the centre.

As a well-established Ballymun arts venue, Axis offers a convenient single location for children interested in performance, whether through acting, traditional Irish dance or classical ballet training.

Sport Taekwondo Ireland's Ballymun club teaches taekwondo to children aged 5 and up at Trinity Comprehensive School on Ballymun Road, Dublin 11.

Classes run on Monday and Wednesday evenings, giving students two sessions a week to build technique, fitness and discipline through this Korean martial art.

The open-ended age range from 5 upward means both younger children and older students can train together or progress through belt levels as part of the same club.

Ballymun Boxing Club runs junior boxing sessions at Poppintree Community Sports Centre on Balbutcher Lane in Ballymun, Dublin 9.

Sessions take place on Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 6pm, giving young boxers a regular twice-weekly training routine focused on fitness, technique and discipline.

As a community boxing club, it offers local children a structured introduction to the sport in a well-established Ballymun sports facility.
